newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WRIGHT APOLOGISES FOR BRANDING PLEAT A PERVERT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WRIGHT APOLOGISES FOR BRANDING PLEAT A PERVERT.

text.p: England striker Ian Wright has apologised to Sheffield Wednesday manager David Pleat for branding him a pervert.
"It was just a joke. I didn't think it would come out that way," Wright said in a television interview on Monday.
Wright made the "pervert" jibe after Pleat protested to the Football Association (F.A.) for two alleged incidents involving the Arsenal forward in a recent premier league game at Highbury.
Pleat called for an inquiry after Wright was caught on television pulling the dreadlocks of Wednesday's Regi Blinker and stamping on defender Dejan Stefanovic.

The F.A. have written to Wright asking him to explain his comments, reported in the Daily Mail, which referred to newspaper revelations nine years ago that Pleat was cautioned by police three times for kerb-crawling.
The publicity forced him to resign as Tottenham manager.
Wright told Sky TV on Monday: "It (the pervert comment) was said in a jovial manner at the end of a very long day. People were firing all sorts of questions and I didn't think it would be published.
"It was not meant to offend anyone and I can't apologise enough. I have spoken to David Pleat and I'm very pleased that he accepted my apology."
